name: Zen Anti-Drone System

header.one_liner: Hyderabad-built layered counter-UAS with RF jamming + kinetic/net hard-kill; in Indian Air Force service since 2021 with multiple follow-on contracts.
header.indigenous_label: AS9100D / CMMI Level 5 certified; ~90%+ indigenous on simulators; EO/IR and RF detector SDR front-ends imported

at_a_glance.Detection_range_radar: X-band 3D radar; engagement range up to 20 km (vendor claim)
at_a_glance.Hard_kill_options: Kinetic (auto-aligned gun) OR net-based interceptor drone (Zen ADS-HK)
at_a_glance.Operational_with: Indian Air Force, Indian Army (Army Air Defence College Gopalpur since mid-2024)

what_it_is.prose: The Zen Anti-Drone System (ZADS) is a layered counter-UAS platform designed and manufactured by Zen Technologies Limited of Hyderabad. The system integrates an X-band 3D radar, a passive RF direction finder and classification system (RFDD), a Video-based Drone Identification and Tracking (VDIT) module with up to 3 km tracking range, a Drone Direction-Finding Control Centre (DFCC), and a Drone RF Jammer (DRFJ) that simultaneously jams ISM bands, GNSS, mobile signals and intercepted frequencies with effective jamming range up to 4 km. The hard-kill configuration, marketed as Zen ADS-HK, offers two effectors: a kinetic option in which an auto-aligned gun engages the target, and a net-based interceptor drone that captures the rogue drone and lands it safely for forensic analysis. The 'V3' label used in the Atlas is an editorial designation; Zen's official product page markets the system simply as 'Zen Anti Drone System (CUAS)' without a version number. Wikipedia notes a May 2026 radar update targeting swarm and FPV drone threats. ZADS entered Indian Air Force service in 2021 as part of more than ₹300 crore in armed forces orders, with follow-on orders in September 2023, November 2025 (₹289 crore) and January 2026 (₹404 crore including simulators). Hard-kill variants were delivered to the Army Air Defence College at Gopalpur from mid-2024.

stages.label: Defeat
stages.note: DRFJ soft-kill jammer (4 km); kinetic gun OR net interceptor hard-kill (ADS-HK)

deployments_procurement.summary: ZADS entered operational service with the Indian Air Force in 2021 as part of more than ₹300 crore in armed forces orders. The Ministry of Defence placed a follow-on procurement order in September 2023, followed by a ₹289 crore counter-drone contract in November 2025 and a ₹404 crore defence orders package (including ₹332 crore for anti-drone systems plus ₹72 crore for simulators) in January 2026. Hard-kill variants were delivered to the Indian Army's Army Air Defence College at Gopalpur from mid-2024, indicating the system is in service with both the IAF and the Army.

import_dependencies.summary: Zen Technologies is AS9100D, ISO/IEC 27001, and CMMI Maturity Level 5 certified, with approximately 90%+ indigenous content on its simulator product line. For the ZADS counter-UAS platform specifically, the principal imported subsystems are EO/IR gimbals and thermal imaging cores (typically sourced from Teledyne FLIR, Controp, or SCD — USA / Israel / Belgium), RF detector SDR front-ends (Ettus / National Instruments / RTL-SDR — USA / Taiwan), and FPGA for signal processing (Xilinx / AMD — USA). The 12.7 mm heavy machine gun used in the kinetic hard-kill variant is a domestically-produced or licensed-pattern weapon.

faq.question: What is the Zen ADS-HK variant?
faq.answer: ADS-HK is Zen Technologies' hard-kill configuration of the ZADS platform. It offers two effectors: a kinetic option in which an auto-aligned gun engages the target, and a net-based interceptor drone (dedicated interceptor with hanging net) that captures the rogue drone and lands it safely for forensic analysis. The ADS-HK variant was delivered to the Indian Army's Army Air Defence College at Gopalpur from mid-2024.

faq.question: What does the 'V3' label mean?
faq.answer: The 'V3' label is an Atlas editorial designation. Zen Technologies' official product page markets the system simply as 'Zen Anti Drone System (CUAS)' without a version number. The vendor has not publicly versioned the platform; the May 2026 radar update for swarm and FPV threats represents the latest publicly-known product evolution.

faq.question: What is the relationship between ZADS and the Zen ADS-HK variant?
faq.answer: ZADS (Zen Anti-Drone System) is the base layered counter-UAS platform. Zen ADS-HK is the hard-kill configuration of ZADS, offering two effectors: a kinetic option in which an auto-aligned gun engages the target, and a net-based interceptor drone (a dedicated interceptor with hanging net) that captures the rogue drone and lands it safely for forensic analysis. The ADS-HK variant was delivered to the Indian Army's Army Air Defence College at Gopalpur from mid-2024, indicating that the Indian Army has operationally deployed both soft-kill and hard-kill ZADS configurations.
